name: NY-11

District leans Republican by 10 points on PVI

model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Malliotakis: a 10-point Republican-leaning district, incumbency, and a roughly 40-to-1 fundraising advantage, with markets giving DeCillis about a 4% chance. With no polling to contradict that picture, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin near R+15.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the challenger within single digits, or a major late outside-spending intervention, would be the first sign this is closer than it looks.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nicole Malliotakis seeks a fourth term in a Staten Island-based district that leans Republican by about ten points. She enters with a commanding financial position, having raised $2.75 million and holding $2.77 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Michael DeCillis has raised only about $68,000. No outside groups are meaningfully engaged on either side.

Prediction markets give DeCillis roughly a 4% chance of an upset, and no public polls of the race are available. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the money gap makes Malliotakis a clear favorite, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
